sections.h2: Which office takes deeds for Kane County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Deeds for property in Kane County are recorded with the Kane County Recorder at 719 S. Batavia Avenue, Building C, in Geneva, IL 60134, phone (630) 232-5935. The office posts a price schedule, a land records search, forms, and an eRecording page on its own website, kanecountyrecorder.net.

Kane County sits along the Fox River west of Chicago, and a deed for a house in Aurora, Elgin, Batavia, St. Charles or a smaller village is recorded in the same Geneva office. Recording puts the new owner on the public record, and the title company or attorney handling your closing normally takes care of it. A seller who is conveying without a title company, such as a family transfer, should know the filing rules below before going to the counter.

sections.h2: How much does the Kane County Recorder charge?
sections.html:
A standard real estate document costs $99.00 to record under the price schedule effective October 1, 2024, and a standard non real estate document costs $80.00. The schedule cites 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.1, the Illinois law that sets a single predictable fee for recording.

Kane County Recorder price schedule effective October 1, 2024
ItemFee
Standard real estate related document$99.00
Standard non real estate document$80.00
Non-conforming document$121.00
Plat of survey (one page, 11 x 17, up to two lots)$99.00
Subdivision or townhouse plat$127.00
UCC financing statement$97.00
Certified copy, first 4 pages$80.00
Photo copy, per page$1.00

The recorder accepts cash or a check made payable to Kane County Recorder, and the schedule says overages on checks are not returned. Fees above are for recording only. Any Illinois transfer tax due on a sale is a separate charge.

sections.h2: Why did the Kane County recording fee change in 2024?
sections.html:
The county board raised the GIS fee collected on each recorded document from $26 to $48, effective October 1, 2024, after a cost study. The recorder keeps $1 of that amount and $47 goes into the GIS Fee Fund that supports the countywide Geographic Information System.

The same notice sets the standard recording price at $99. The increase was adopted by Kane County Board Resolution 24-362 on September 10, 2024, under 55 ILCS 5/3-5018. Anyone using an older price list from a title packet, a form site or a past closing should check the current schedule before writing a check.

sections.h2: What makes a deed non-conforming in Kane County?
sections.html:
A document that breaks the state's standard form rules pays the non-conforming price of $121.00 instead of $99.00. The schedule reproduces the standards that Illinois law requires, and they are simple enough to check before you print.

  • One or more loose sheets of 8.5 by 11 inches, not permanently bound and not a continuous form. Graphics up to 11 by 17 inches record without extra charge.
  • Legible black ink, by hand, type or computer. Signatures and dates may be in contrasting colors if they reproduce clearly.
  • White paper of at least 20-pound weight with a clean half inch margin on every side.
  • A blank space of at least 3 by 5 inches in the upper right corner of the first page, which the recorder uses for the stamp.
  • Nothing stapled or otherwise attached to any page.

More than five parcel numbers or more than five referenced document numbers on one document also triggers the non-conforming price.

sections.h2: What about Illinois transfer tax on a Kane County sale?
sections.html:
State transfer tax is collected by the county recorder at 50 cents per $500 of value, or fraction of $500, under 35 ILCS 200/31-15. Paper revenue stamps were to be phased out by December 31, 2025, and after that counties issue electronic stamps or another indicator.

Every recorded sale also has to be reported to the Illinois Department of Revenue through its electronic MyDec system, whether or not a stamp is used. That filing is the transfer declaration the recorder asks for with a deed. Some deeds are exempt from the tax itself under 35 ILCS 200/31-45, including tax deeds, deeds that release security for a debt, deeds where the consideration is under $100, and deeds to a mortgage holder in a foreclosure or in lieu transfer. Some of those still require the declaration to be filed. If your county or municipality charges an additional local transfer tax, ask the Kane County Recorder and the city or village clerk for the current rate before closing, because this page does not set it.

sections.h2: Can I record a deed electronically in Kane County?
sections.html:
Yes. Kane County accepts electronic recording through three approved vendors, Corporation Service Company, Simplifile and Hopdox, and the recorder asks you to contact a vendor to compare prices and enroll. Paper documents are scanned into the recording system, and plats are not accepted for eRecording.

The recorder's page says electronic submission cuts processing to minutes, reduces rejections for wrong fees, and lets a corrected document be resubmitted in hours instead of days. Title companies and law offices usually use these vendors. An individual doing a one-time family transfer usually delivers paper to the Geneva office with the correct fee.

sections.h2: How do I find out whether a deed was recorded on my property?
sections.html:
Kane County runs a free Land Records Search on the recorder's website, and it also mails a postcard whenever a deed is recorded. The green Property Transfer Notification postcard goes to the grantor, shows a document number, and lists a number to call if the owner did not know about the transaction. No sign-up is needed.

This feature is useful to a seller who wants proof that the buyer's deed was recorded after closing, and to an owner who worries about deed fraud. The recorder also offers a Personal Information Redaction Request form and a Copy Center order form for copies sent by mail.

sections.h2: Are there copy and special document fees in Kane County?
sections.html:
Copies cost $1.00 per photo copy page, and a certified copy costs $80.00 for the first four pages and $1.00 for each additional page. Plat copies run $5.00 for the first page, then $2.00 a page, with a certified plat copy at $10.00. Fax and email copies run $5.00 for the first page and $1.00 for each added page.

Veterans get a break on military discharge papers. A DD214 brought in by the veteran, the veteran's family or a Veterans Administration representative is recorded with no charge and includes four certified copies, while a commercial third party pays $80.00. A condominium declaration recorded with its plat is priced at $149.00, with the map at $50 for the first page and $1 for each page after.

sections.h2: What does Census data show about Kane County property?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 184,706 households in Kane County for 2020 to 2024 and 195,957 housing units as of July 2025. About 76.0 percent of homes are owner occupied, and 90.1 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier.

Homes owned by their occupants have a $327,000 median value, and 1,629 building permits were issued in 2025. If a prior deed was never recorded, a title company or attorney can explain how to fix the chain before you list.

faqs.q: What is the fee for a Kane County deed?
faqs.a: Recording a standard real estate document costs $99.00 under the schedule effective October 1, 2024. A non-conforming document costs $121.00, and the recorder accepts cash or checks payable to Kane County Recorder.
Yes, through Corporation Service Company, Simplifile and Hopdox. Plats cannot be recorded electronically, and paper documents can still be brought to the recorder in Geneva.

faqs.q: What is the Illinois transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The state collects 50 cents for every $500 of value or fraction of $500 under 35 ILCS 200/31-15. Ask the recorder about any local tax before closing, and expect to file the MyDec declaration.

faqs.q: Can I check that my deed was recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. Use the free Land Records Search on the Kane County Recorder's website, or watch for the green transfer notification postcard mailed to the grantor after a deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Why was my deed rejected in Kane County?
faqs.a: Ask the Kane County Recorder at (630) 232-5935 for the reason. The office publishes a Rejections page, and an incorrect fee or a document that misses the form standards, such as staples, bound pages or no blank space on the first page, are the issues its price schedule and eRecording page point to.
